findings.claim: One user says they hand write release notes and copy-paste version numbers for each release.

quotes.text: I hand write the release notes, copy and paste the version number, and select date for each release (sometimes I'll batch add them if I get behind).

findings.reason: The quote directly states the user hands writes release notes and copies version numbers, matching the claim exactly.
findings.limitations: Single user experience, not generalizable to all users.

findings.claim: One user says they hand author release notes in a Django admin for a /release-notes/ page.

quotes.text: Clicking that takes the user to a /release-notes/ page that has a descending order list of the notes that I hand author in the Django admin.

findings.claim: One user says they use GitHub generated release notes from Pull Request bodies for their dev team.

quotes.text: I use Github generated release notes based on Pull Request bodies and this is more than sufficient for my dev team.

findings.reason: The quote directly states that the user uses GitHub generated release notes from Pull Request bodies for their dev team, matching the claim exactly.
findings.limitations: Limited to one user's experience, not generalizability.

findings.claim: One user says they have to manually check release notes for accuracy before publishing.

quotes.text: Because of this it's tricky to fully automate the process as at some level you usually need a person casting an eye over the release note just to sense check.

findings.claim: Small software teams spend too much time writing release notes and changelogs.

quotes.text: I use Github generated release notes based on Pull Request bodies and this is more than sufficient for my dev team.

findings.reason: The quote states that using GitHub-generated release notes from PRs is sufficient for the speaker's small dev team, but the context specifies it's for internal apps, not public SaaS, so it doesn't directly address the claim about small software teams in general.
findings.limitations: Only applies to internal apps, not public SaaS teams.
review: wording goes beyond the quoted text: spend, too, much, time, writing, changelogs
a claim about people must be attributed to one person ("One host says ...")
